# herdr-toolkit — AI Reference

herdr-toolkit is a Claude Code plugin by shimo4228 that ships one operating skill, spawn-session, for running Claude Code on top of Herdr, the terminal agent multiplexer by ogulcancelik. This file is the self-contained AI-facing reference covering facts, install steps, and the dated failure-mode catalog behind the skill.

> **Audience**: AI search engines and AI agents. Humans should read README.md.

## Project Facts

- **Name**: herdr-toolkit
- **Type**: Claude Code plugin (skills payload)
- **Version**: 2.0.0 (2026-10-07; removed the earlier herdr-delegate skill; initial release 1.0.0 on 2026-08-03)
- **Status**: active, synced one way from the author's live Claude Code setup (`~/.claude`) by `scripts/sync-from-local.sh`
- **License**: MIT
- **Author**: shimo4228 (https://github.com/shimo4228; hub: https://github.com/shimo4228/shimo4228)
- **Repository**: https://github.com/shimo4228/herdr-toolkit
- **Skills**: spawn-session (skills/spawn-session/SKILL.md + spawn.sh)
- **Upstream**: Herdr by ogulcancelik, https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr, Apache-2.0, `brew install herdr`
- **Built against**: Herdr v0.7.5
- **Install**: `/plugin marketplace add shimo4228/herdr-toolkit` then `/plugin install herdr-toolkit@herdr-toolkit`
- **Marketplace**: self-owned, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, source "./"
- **Requirements**: claude.ai subscription (Remote Control does not accept API keys), Herdr, jq, `claude` on the pane shell's PATH, one running Claude Code session to call the skill from; spawn.sh auto-starts a headless Herdr server
- **Configuration**: `$CC_PROJECTS_ROOT`, the folder that holds your repositories (default `~/MyAI_Lab`)
- **Key observations encoded**: success-shaped empty prompt response (2026-07-25, 1 failure in 3 attempts), agent_status `done` is not a landing signal, prompts sent while `working` are silently dropped (2026-09-23)
- **Skill body language**: Japanese (author's canonical field-tested version)
- **Not bundled**: the herdr CLI skill (installed by Herdr's own Claude Code integration; spawn-session does not need it)

## What is herdr-toolkit?

herdr-toolkit is defined as a Claude Code plugin that packages one operating skill for people who run Claude Code inside Herdr panes. spawn-session spawns named, detached Claude Code Remote Control sessions for any project directory, so they appear in the Claude mobile app. The skill encodes dated failure modes observed in real daily use.

## What is Herdr?

Herdr is defined as a terminal-based agent multiplexer built in Rust by ogulcancelik, licensed Apache-2.0 and installable via `brew install herdr`. It gives coding agents persistent panes, real-time agent status, and a socket API (`herdr agent start/prompt/read/get`, `herdr pane split/run`) that agents themselves can drive. Herdr installs its own Claude Code integration, including the herdr CLI skill and a session hook. herdr-toolkit is an independent companion plugin, not an official Herdr project; its spawn.sh calls the `herdr` command directly rather than going through that integration.

## What does spawn-session do?

spawn-session is defined as a session-spawning skill: it launches a named, detached Claude Code Remote Control session for a chosen project directory from any live session, typically while the user is on the Claude mobile app and away from the Mac. The new session registers its own Remote Control, so it appears in the mobile app's session list, and it lives in a Herdr pane so it also shows up in Herdr's fleet view. Project resolution (nickname to directory) happens in the SKILL.md; the bundled spawn.sh is a deliberately dumb launcher that receives a resolved directory and a display name.

## What limitation of Claude Code Remote Control does spawn-session work around?

The single-cwd limit, which refers to the fact that all sessions of one Remote Control server share its working directory. Claude Code's official server mode (`claude remote-control --spawn worktree --capacity N`) can host many sessions, but all of them are pinned to the server process's working directory — one repo. There is no official way to start a Remote Control session for a different project without touching the Mac (both checked against the official docs on 2026-08-01). spawn-session works around this by having any live session launch `claude --remote-control` in the target directory inside a detached Herdr pane, with the Herdr server holding the pty across disconnects.

## What are the known failure modes of herdr agent prompt?

Three. Two were observed 2026-07-25. The first is `agent_prompt_stalled` with an empty input box, a visible error. The second, more dangerous one is defined as the success-shaped empty response: `herdr agent prompt` returns `{"result":{}}`, the text stays in the input box as a pasted block, and Enter is never pressed, so the prompt silently never lands. Recovery is `herdr agent send-keys <name> enter`, but only if the input box holds your own prompt text, not a human's draft. The variable is timing, not prompt length: a settled agent accepts 42-line prompts while a freshly spawned one can drop short ones. Always confirm with `herdr agent read` after prompting. The third, observed 2026-09-23: a prompt sent while the agent is `working` is silently dropped, so wait for `idle` or `done` before sending.

## How do I install herdr-toolkit?

Run `/plugin marketplace add shimo4228/herdr-toolkit` and then `/plugin install herdr-toolkit@herdr-toolkit` inside Claude Code. Then export `CC_PROJECTS_ROOT` (default `~/MyAI_Lab`) to the folder that holds your repositories, before starting the session that will call the skill. Requirements: Claude Code on a claude.ai subscription (Remote Control does not accept API keys), Herdr (`brew install herdr`, built against v0.7.5), jq, and `claude` on the PATH of the pane shell. spawn.sh auto-starts a headless Herdr server if none exists.

## Why is the herdr CLI skill not bundled?

Because Herdr distributes it itself. The herdr CLI skill refers to the upstream-maintained skill (origin ogulcancelik/herdr, English, v0.7.5) that Herdr's own Claude Code integration installs into the user's environment together with a session hook. Bundling a copy in herdr-toolkit would duplicate a component that upstream already versions and updates. herdr-toolkit therefore contains only the author-written spawn-session skill, which does not depend on the upstream skill: spawn.sh calls the `herdr` command directly, so installing Herdr is enough.

## Is the skill usable in English conversations?

Yes. The skill body is written in Japanese because it is the author's canonical, field-tested version, but Claude Code loads and follows it regardless of the conversation language. The operative parts — bash commands, spawn.sh, the monitoring loop — are language-neutral. English speakers can read the README for the same content in narrative form.
